A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Zero-Inflated Bandits, with matching core models, algorithms and MAB theorems. All 46 pages of v1 and 60 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1–3 report original Gaussian, mixed-Gaussian and exponential MAB simulations with 50 replications.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original MAB and contextual simulations, loan-data-based counterfactual experiments, and offline model-fit analyses.

M1.justification: The product framework remains, but contextual UCB Algorithm 5 changes materially as written: the nonzero-part ridge update becomes a g-based optimization, and the binary selection-index factor loses its h link. v2 also adds exploration initialization and a Huber-regression adaptation for the loan experiment.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only synthetic MABs. v2 adds contextual-bandit simulations and an auto-loan pricing task using 208,085 records to construct a simulator. The three MAB distribution families remain, with revised sparsity ranges and an extreme zero-inflation scenario.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates misspecified UCB, integrated UCB, misspecified TS and integrated TS in contextual and loan experiments. The Gaussian/mixed-Gaussian MAB comparator set remains. MOTS disappears from reported exponential comparisons, although Appendix B.1 retains CMS-adaptation text.

E3.justification: Standard MAB horizons change from 50,000 to 75,000 rounds. New contextual simulations use 100 arms, 10-dimensional features and 20,000 rounds; the loan simulator uses five actions and 5,000 rounds. Figure 6's extreme-sparsity horizon is unresolved: its caption says 10,000, but its axis reaches 100,000.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's probability sweeps and proxy illustrations, v2 adds extreme-sparsity testing, contextual sparsity sweeps, Monte Carlo comparisons of concentration-bound tightness, and loan-model link, feature-transformation and noise-sensitivity analyses. Figure 10 also adds numerical derivative diagnostics.

E5.justification: MAB simulations retain 50 replications; new contextual simulations specify 25. v2 adds FDR estimation using data splitting in Table 2 and uses regret error bars instead of v1's shaded bands. Neither version clearly defines the plotted uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: v2 adds contextual and loan regret curves, bound-tightness results, FDR values and coefficient-sensitivity results. Table 2 reports 0.1831 for linear/logit and 0.0983 for linear/log. MAB curves use revised horizons and sparsity settings, and exponential TS results are removed; these changes do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds contextual Theorem 4 with regularity assumptions and Appendix G's derivation, Corollary 1 comparing product and standard UCB bounds, and a posterior-factorization derivation. Lemma 4(i) expands from p = 1/2 to any p in (0,1). The main MAB theorems remain, but v1's explicit problem-independent light-tailed UCB derivation is omitted.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions expand from MAB guarantees and simulations to contextual-GLM guarantees and empirical evidence using real data. v2 newly claims the first finite-sample concentration analysis of ZI models even outside bandits. Table 1 distinguishes minimax-optimal, near-optimal and state-of-the-art guarantees more explicitly.

C2.justification: The central efficiency explanation remains. v2 revises the rationale for Beta clipping from consistency to controlling product overestimation, explains why exponential TS comparisons are omitted, and cautions that favorable loan-data performance of misspecified methods need not generalize.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds hardware and runtimes, contextual parameter generation and tuning, loan features and price construction, action thresholds, counterfactual-generation procedures, and data-access-upon-request instructions. v1's heuristic guidance for estimating tail and size parameters from historical data is removed.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands connections to contextual-GLM and heavy-tailed bandits, dynamic pricing, auto lending and statistical inference. Related work newly contrasts its bandit analysis with offline zero-inflated modeling, citing Lambert, Hall and Cheung, and broadens the concentration-analysis novelty claim.

P1.justification: The introduction, method motivation, theory exposition and discussion are extensively rewritten. Several algorithms and the RGBO formulation move to appendices, while new algorithm and experimental appendices precede reorganized proofs. These changes substantially alter the narrative beyond adding scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 adds theoretical-summary and FDR tables and new motivation, contextual and loan figures. MAB panels gain shared legends, dashed method lines and error bars. The earlier proxy surfaces are redrawn and consolidated into Figure 10 with derivative panels, and several algorithms move to full-width appendix displays.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's lack of contextual evaluation and practical-data evidence, while Appendix B substantially improves reproducibility information. However, the new contextual proof has a substantive gap: Appendix G, Step 2.3 infers separate factorwise maximization from Algorithm 5's product maximization, which does not imply it. Figure 6 also introduces contradictory horizon reporting. The substantial empirical and documentation gains coexist with concerns about a new central theoretical claim, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
